title: Generate Valid Feature Configurations
real_world_story: An AI platform has several optional modules, but some configurations must satisfy a required number of enabled modules. The configuration engine needs to generate valid combinations of modules.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Available feature modules and the required number of active modules
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Backtracking to explore possible selections while constructing valid combinations

problem_statement: Given N distinct feature IDs and an integer K, generate all combinations containing exactly K features. Print the number of valid configurations.
task: Determine how many different configurations containing exactly K features can be created from N available features.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and K. The second line contains N space-separated distinct feature IDs.
output_format: Print the number of valid configurations containing exactly K features.

examples.explanation: There are six ways to choose exactly two features from four features.
There are ten possible configurations containing exactly three of the five features.

expected_algorithm.name: Backtracking
expected_algorithm.reason: Backtracking explores the available feature choices and constructs configurations containing exactly K selected features.

complexity.where: C(N,K) is the number of valid K-element combinations.

hint: At every step, decide whether to include the current feature.
Stop exploring a branch when it cannot produce K selected features.
Count every configuration containing exactly K features.
Backtracking allows the search space to be explored systematically.
real_world_takeaway: Backtracking is useful when an AI configuration system must explore possible combinations while satisfying a fixed configuration requirement.
